title: Segmented shingle-based prefix cache and deterministic fingerprinting for embeddings & reranker
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: The embeddings + reranking endpoint sees repeated duplicate and near-duplicate inputs (URL fragments, boilerplate headers, user signatures) that inflate compute and increase tail latency. Current prefix-caching approaches reduce token re-encode but suffer from false misses when content is semantically equivalent but lexically different (whitespace, punctuation, small edits). Additionally, cache invalidation after dataset updates or model reindex is noisy — full flushes are costly and cause a high cold-start tax for heavy tenants.
objectives: Decrease median + p95 embedding compute for rerank workloads by >= 40% for sessions with repeat/near-duplicate content
Reduce cache footprint using deduplication of semantically equivalent prefixes (target 2-3x effective dedupe)
Provide deterministic, auditable invalidation semantics tied to collection/model version changes
Support tenant isolation (no cross-tenant pollution) and fast per-tenant warmup
proposal_summary: Introduce a segmented prefix caching layer that fingerprints normalized text via a shingled hashing pipeline (normalize -> stemming-lite -> stopword trim -> 3-gram shingle -> signed 64-bit rolling hash). Cache keys include tenant id, model id + model fingerprint, shard id, and shingle fingerprint. Store both exact-embed and deduplicated-index entries. Add a versioned invalidation token mapped to collection/model rollouts to support targeted eviction without global flushes.
design_decisions: Normalization: apply NFKC unicode normalization, collapse whitespace, lowercase, canonicalize URLs (strip tracking params), and remove common boilerplate headers (config-driven)
Shingling: 3-token overlapping shingles to capture local context; trade-off chosen after offline eval between 2 vs 3 vs 4 for recall/dedupe
Hashing: farmhash-compatible 64-bit rolling hash with salt derived from tenant+model to avoid collisions across tenants
Cache layout: segmented by tenant and model fingerprint; within segment maintain two maps: shingle->canonical-key, canonical-key->embedding-ref
Eviction: cost-aware LRU with size buckets (small, medium, large embeddings) and a hot-prefetch counter to avoid evicting recently warm entries
Invalidation: maintain a per-segment 'generation' token; when model/index changes increment generation and atomically mark old generation for background TTL-based drain instead of immediate purges
Prefetching: optimistic prewarm for tenants hitting new model version using recent request traces (controlled by rate limits)
Fallbacks: on hash collision or low-confidence dedupe, fall back to full embedding compute and write back canonical mapping asynchronously to avoid blocking requests
tradeoffs_and_risks: Increased CPU cost on normalization/shingle hashing path — mitigated by implementing native C++ path and SSE optimizations
Potential for semantic misses for long-range paraphrases that shingle approach won’t dedupe — addressed by adding optional semantic fingerprint step (slow, run in background) for cold dedupe
Risk of incorrect canonicalization for edge-case locale-specific scripts — added integration tests and opt-out per-tenant normalization rules
Operational complexity of per-tenant segments increases metadata overhead — we will shard segments and aggregate metrics to reduce control-plane pressure
performance_targets: Median inference tokens saved: >= 45% on corpora with repeated templates
p95 latency reduction for rerank endpoint: >= 25% under typical load profiles
Cache hit effective dedupe ratio: >= 2.0 (unique inputs vs stored embeddings) for targeted tenants
Cold-start penalty after model rollout: < 15% increased token compute compared to full flush baseline
implementation_plan: Week 1: PoC native shingle hashing library + normalization module (unit tests + microbenchmarks)
Week 2: Integrate into prefix cache read path; add canonicalization table and write-behind async updater
Week 3: Add per-segment generation tokens and invalidation APIs; implement background drain worker
Week 4: End-to-end benchmarks with synthetic traces (templates + paraphrase mix); tune eviction buckets
Week 5: Canary rollout to 2 pilot tenants; collect quality and latency metrics; manual QA of edge cases
Week 6: Expand rollout, add prewarm controls and dashboarding; ship runtime-1.21
Post-release: Monitor for 2 weeks, iterate on normalization rules and semantic dedupe thresholds
acceptance_criteria: Automated unit + integration tests covering normalization corner-cases
Benchmarks demonstrating targets in performance_targets met on two separate datasets
Canary tenants observe no >5% drop in reranking precision (measured via held-out eval prompts) after dedupe enabled
No regressions in throughput under load tests; observability hooks emitting dedupe/hit/miss metrics
Docs PR and runbook for operators describing generation token lifecycle and how to force-drain segments
qa_and_experiment_plan: Create AB test: control (current prefix cache) vs experiment (shingle dedupe) with traffic split 90/10 during canary
Evaluation metrics: rerank nDCG@10, recall@50 for similarity retrievals, end-to-end latency, tokens per query cost
Synthetic adversarial set: fuzzed input corpus with URL variants, signatures, and paraphrases to measure false merges
Manual review of merged-cases subset for business-critical tenants (legal, finance datasets)
rollout_and_migration: Default off for existing tenants; opt-in toggle in tenant config with telemetry
During model reindex, controller will: (1) create new generation token, (2) start prewarm workers, (3) after warm threshold, switch read path to new generation
Provide API to force-drain old generation per-tenant for emergency invalidation
Compatibility: ensure that Dedicated/private deployments can opt for 'lite' normalization rules to comply with PII removal policies
observability_and_metrics: End-to-end latency histograms broken down by hit/miss and by generation
Alert: sustained dedupe_hit_rate drop >30% for 5m or dedupe_false_positive_rate >0.1%
